audit_evidence.summary:
Evidence map built from README §0-4, HANDOFF ch. 5-7, 8.3-8.5, 11.8-11.11 and 12.C, docs/v11/REPORT_I58_v11.md with Appendix C.1-C.4, docs/v11 probe and judge JSONs, results/runs_summary.md, and two server summaries (work/runs/summary_all/summary.md, work/runs/v11/summary/summary.md). I also ran three read-only server checks: which runs have qc_fine.json or export/ (the brainstem pair only), whether the E1 or E2 runs exist (they do not), and work/v11/tests/mask_I46/result.json.

WHAT THE EVIDENCE SUPPORTS AS A GENERAL METHOD. A short core has real support across more than one dataset:
- training-free two-class structure maps, with the MRI flattened by a local tissue mean;
- exhaustive FFT masked-NCC search over rotations x handedness x class polarity;
- polarity decided by the refined NCC;
- a clamped rigid -> similarity -> affine ladder with an absolute scale prior.
This core is what placed I46 and I55 (the only quantitatively confirmed subjects) and the brainstem body. The scale prior is also what stopped the shrink degeneracy on the brainstem.

WHAT IS DATASET-SPECIFIC OR NEGATIVE.
- Vascular channel: helps exactly one subject (I46: 12 um OCT with a wrong depth sidecar; ves_seg median 265 -> 167 um; controls collapse the gain). It is silent on I55, has no usable signal on the seven 30-35 um subjects (vessel NCC <= 0.053) and is harmful on the brainstem (2.65 mm move, 4778 s). The depth-scale story is n=1 each way, and I55 recovers 6/7.
- v1.1 texture mask: works on agarose, but on I46 it keeps 0.28 of the 0.68 cm3 cortex mask. Only a volume-ratio switch keeps it off DANDI.
- v1.1 fine stage: rejected on I58 in all 13 runs or configurations, and accepted-but-harmful on cortex (I46 vesseg 167 -> 264 um, stretch 1.219 -> 1.31; I55 GM Dice 0.930 -> 0.916).
- Clear negatives: nonrigid, parser, self-distillation, MIND, raw intensity, and the P5-P11 objectives (surface distance, MI, piecewise, exclusion, renormalisation).
- QC: restarts are anti-correlated with correctness (I58 and I61 at 12/12 are wrong; I46 and I55 are 9/12). The search margin also flags I55 and the brainstem. Absolute NCC is meaningless across subjects. Boundary-agreement and MI-landscape QC were only ever computed on the brainstem, were never calibrated, and give conflicting answers on its handedness.

UNSOLVED GENERAL PROBLEM. Foreground separation (MRI bath, OCT agarose) is behind I61, DANDI I58, I56's broken mask and the brainstem mask excess (>= 5.5 cm3 non-tissue). The current handling is two different rules: a fail-open histogram rule and a texture mode behind an auto switch. Sectioning artefacts are also handled by two overlapping steps: slab normalisation hard-coded to array axis 0 with a window wrong by about 3x, and a separate axis-detected destripe. Neither step has an ablation on registration accuracy.

SCORECARD. On the nine DANDI subjects: 2 confirmed (I46, I55); 3 unresolved (I38, I56, I62 rest on unverified AI-made figures, with annotations 55-66 mm away in a label frame known to be broken); 1 undecidable (I48, margin 0.0013); 3 failed (I61 mask; DANDI I58 at 10 deg flip angle; I57 undiagnosed). I57's "wrong" verdict has the same weight of evidence as I38's "correct" until map_labels_to_grid is fixed.

REPRODUCIBILITY. The v1 snapshot reproduces I46 and I55 exactly, and v1.1 defaults give 0/26 regression failures on each. The brainstem one-command run reproduces R5 to 0.00 mm. The other seven DANDI subjects were never re-run on the current tree.

WHAT A REVIEWER WILL ASK FOR THAT IS MISSING.
1. Baselines: Costantini B0 (approximable), masked-MI multi-start affine (B1), ANTs/NiftyReg, MIND+ConvexAdam, generalist nets. None has been run.
2. TRE: none on any pair. No landmarks requested; the authors' I46 affine sits 23 mm from ours, unresolved.
3. Registration-level ablations of bias flattening, slab normalisation, the masks, destripe, the DOF ladder and the scale-prior values. Feature, mirror and vessel ablations exist on I46 only (40 mm crop).
4. Sensitivity: n_rot, search level, topk/NMS, reg/clamp, overlap constants, metadata spacing (I46 at 14 um / I55 at 12 um), seeds on DANDI, noise/resolution, block size (0.09-7.19 % of the hemisphere), flip angle (I58 at 30 deg).
5. Controls: a true random-pose control. A synthetic known-transform benchmark for capture range and accuracy.
6. Evaluation fixes: correct label mapping for the six 0.12 mm subjects, a rotation metric that works for mirrored transforms, human-verified figures, and more labelled subjects (I45, I60 carry ves_seg).
7. Runtime and memory for the final method on every pair. Current evidence: 18.7-131 min on DANDI, with the vascular stage taking up to 72-91 % of wall time; 27.6 min and 32 GB peak on the brainstem; no v1.1 runtime table across all pairs.
8. Complexity: 49 register.py flags, 27 prep flags and 74 scripts. More than half of the flags belong to components the evidence says to drop (fine, polish, vascular gate, mask sub-options, parser, nonrigid).

items.name: Two-class structure maps (flattened Otsu, soft sigmoid, both OCT polarities)
items.where: octreg/features.py (otsu_two_class, otsu_two_class_lowmem); scripts/prep_subject.py; scripts/register.py --features otsu; HANDOFF §5.1, §6.10.9; results/runs_summary.md
items.what: Both volumes reduced to soft [bright, dark] class probability maps inside a tissue mask (Otsu threshold, sigmoid scale 0.25 std); OCT channel 0 is always the bright class and polarity is applied by swapping channels.
items.evidence: I46 crop ablation (40 mm box, runs_summary.md): otsu top1 0.727 / refined 0.753 / restarts 7/8 / Dice 0.801/0.830. Raw intensity: 0.594 / 0.693 / 4/8. Parser: 0.650 / 0.710 / 5/8, 19 mm off. MIND: 0.219 / 0.185 / 3/8, 17.9 mm off. Mixed: 0.733 / 0.731. Whole hemisphere I46_otsu vs I46_parser: same centre to 0.03 mm, refined NCC 0.7564 vs 0.7218. Carried the pose on I46 and I55 (quantitative), on I38/I56/I62 (visual only) and on the brainstem body (v1 NCC 0.1014, channels [-0.017, 0.220]; v1.1 0.1241). Known blind spots: (1) depth scale: along depth dNCC 0.021 vs 0.169 along k over s 0.85-1.30 (scale_profiles.json), and Dice moves 0.007; (2) polarity symmetry at 0.6 mm: the wrong polarity scores 0.7275 vs 0.7273 at a pose 71 mm away; (3) the level is not comparable across subjects (I61 0.502 wrong, I62 0.284 visually correct). Every feature ablation is on one subject.
items.recommendation: Keep as the single representation of the general method. Repeat the otsu vs intensity vs MIND ablation on I55 and the brainstem so it is not n=1, and state the depth-scale and polarity blind spots in the method text.

items.name: MRI bias-field flattening before Otsu
items.where: features.otsu_two_class_lowmem (tissue-weighted local mean, sigma 10 mm, floor 0.5 x p5); HANDOFF §5.1.5, §6.14.2; README §1
items.what: Divide the MRI by a smooth tissue-only local mean before the global Otsu split, so a receive-coil ramp does not become the class boundary.
items.evidence: I46 whole hemisphere vs manual labels (re-derived first-hand, /tmp/flat.py): raw Otsu Dice WM/GM 0.6502/0.5987; flattened 0.9069/0.9343. The intensity ramp is 1.9x (local mean p5 29.3, p95 55.4). A tissue-inverted MRI (crop_final_inv2) still recovers the pose (vessels 179-182 um), but with 0/12 structural restarts (re-parsed twin 8/12). Not measured on I55, not on the 0.12 mm subjects (broken label mapping), and not on the 0.08 mm brainstem crop, where a 10 mm kernel on a ~30-40 mm FOV was never checked. No registration-level with/without ablation exists. The same idea at 3 mm gave the best fine-scale signal on I58 (P2: flattened NCC contrast 0.54 vs raw NCC 0.36).
items.recommendation: Keep, and apply one physical-sigma flattening rule to both modalities. Add a registration-level ablation (flattening off) on I46, I55 and the brainstem, and the segmentation Dice on I55.

items.name: Raw intensity similarity (search or polish)
items.where: features.build_features(kind='intensity'); scripts/test_polish.py; HANDOFF §7.3.4; REPORT P2
items.what: Tissue z-scored intensities correlated directly across modalities.
items.evidence: I46 crop: top1/top2 0.594/0.592 (margin 0.002), refined 0.693, 4/8 restarts, correct centre only inside the crop. Brainstem: cross-modal NCC 0.033 at 0.32 mm and 0.030 at 0.16 mm; the polish dragged a correct pose 9.37 mm (centre) / 9.55 mm (corner mean) / 12.3 mm (corner max). P2: the relation is inverted and not uniform (raw masked NCC -0.23 at the pose; 26/37 sub-blocks negative, range -0.63 to +0.18).
items.recommendation: Drop as an objective. Mention it as a baseline row only.

items.name: MIND-SSC descriptor
items.where: features.mind_ssc; HANDOFF §7.3.5; REPORT P2
items.what: 12-channel modality-independent self-similarity descriptor used as search/refine features.
items.evidence: I46 crop: top1 0.219, the refinement lowered it to 0.185, 3/8 restarts, 17.9 mm corner-mean off (33 mm max), 0 manual vessels inside the block, about 3x slower search (31 s vs 11 s). Brainstem P2: peak-to-shoulder contrast 0.02, no optimum at 0.3 mm.
items.recommendation: Remove from the package. Keep one table row as a standard-descriptor baseline.

items.name: Trained 3D U-Net parser (and synth.py domain randomisation)
items.where: octreg/parser.py, octreg/synth.py, scripts/train_parser.py, parse_mri.py, register.py --features parser
items.what: Supervised WM/infra-GM/supra-GM segmentation used as the structure map.
items.evidence: crop_parser_v2 lands 19 mm off (0.650/0.710, 5/8). crop_parser_v1: wrong pose, scales collapsed to 0.76/0.73/0.77. Whole-hemisphere I46_parser gives the same pose as otsu (0.03 mm) only because the search is robust; its refined NCC 0.7218 is below otsu's 0.7564. Whole-hemisphere parser Dice WM 0.485 / GM 0.586 (logs/parse_I46.log). The claimed 'Dice 0.98' is unverified. parse_mri.py on I56 was OOM-killed. It needs manual whole-hemisphere labels to train, so it cannot run on the brainstem (C-nolabels).
items.recommendation: Remove from the method package and archive. Keep the I46 otsu-vs-parser comparison as a supplementary ablation.

items.name: Cross-modal self-distillation of an OCT parser
items.where: scripts/distill_oct_parser.py; work/runs/summary/distill_log.json; HANDOFF §6.10.8, §7.3.2
items.what: Train an OCT parser on MRI labels pulled through the current transform, re-register, iterate.
items.evidence: Two rounds: top1 0.708 -> 0.874, final NCC 0.724 -> 0.960, self-Dice 0.961, yet the pose moves only 0.51 then 0.68 mm. Vessel median stays 258-265 um / f150 0.27-0.28, against 167 / 0.47 after the vascular stage. Round 0 (MRI parser applied directly to OCT) lands 12.2 mm off.
items.recommendation: Drop. Cite as the cautionary result that internal scores are not accuracy.

items.name: OCT slab normalisation along array axis 0
items.where: common.oct_slab_normalize; prep_subject.py:145 (window = max(10, round(1200/sp_z)) slices along axis 0; fp16 gain 16384/median, cap 60000)
items.what: Per-slice in-tissue median divided by its running mean along the assumed sectioning axis, removing the vibratome sawtooth.
items.evidence: No with/without registration ablation on any subject. The window constant is wrong by about 3x: the measured section period is 33 slices on I46 (window 100 = 3.03 periods, works by luck) and 12 slices on I56 (window 34 = 2.83 periods, residual sawtooth left). On the brainstem the sectioning axis is array axis 2 (P3), so the step runs along an en-face axis. There it removes about 1.5 % (log-scale std 0.015, 85 % of its power on 2.82 mm tile harmonics). Undoing it, or replacing it with per-section normalisation along axis 2 or a 2-D tile flat field, changes structural NCC by <= 0.0004 and moves local refits 0.12-0.55 mm (P11 norm; search and restarts not re-run). The fp16 gain trick is needed engineering: it prevents uint16 overflow to inf, and denormal collapse of the brainstem mu_s map whose raw tissue threshold is 9.6e-4.
items.recommendation: Merge with destripe into one sectioning-artefact step: detected axis, window = measured period. Or drop it if an I46/I55 ablation shows no effect; run that ablation either way. Keep the dtype gain logic as engineering.

items.name: Physical-unit grids and pyramid (pooling to 0.15 mm, levels 0.6/0.3/0.15 mm)
items.where: common.py (layout_affine, pool_mean_np, resample_to_grid, sample_at_world); register.py:122 LEVELS; HANDOFF §5.7
items.what: All kernels, windows, levels, tolerances and learning rates in mm/um. OCT pooled per axis, then resampled onto an exactly isotropic grid in world mm.
items.evidence: The same core flags ran on 0.08, 0.12 and 0.15 mm MRI and 12, 14, 20 and 30-35 um OCT. Search cost scales with the MRI grid (44.8 s on the brainstem crop to 1010 s on I57). Brainstem prep geometry matches the raw file (Spearman 0.940; axis flips <= 0.10; peak at zero shift; C.4). Not sufficient alone: the brainstem still needed pair-specific flags (--vascular off, --skip-vessels, --oct-mask auto, --destripe on). One 'physical' constant (the slab window) is wrong. The 0.6 mm search level and the 0.15 mm finest level were never ablated.
items.recommendation: Keep as a stated design principle. Derive the remaining data-dependent constants (section period, stripe axis) from measurements, not from protocol text.

items.name: OCT intensity tissue mask
items.where: common.histogram_tissue_threshold + oct_tissue_mask (threshold, binary_closing x2, fill holes, largest connected component)
items.what: Foreground (tissue) mask for the OCT block from the intensity histogram, kept to the single largest component.
items.evidence: Adequate on DANDI cortex blocks (no embedding medium; the OCT/MRI volume ratio stays small, so the overlap gate never binds). Never compared with any OCT annotation. Fails on the agarose-embedded brainstem: no histogram valley, threshold falls to the floor, 28.86 cm3 = 77.9 % of the box, 2.17x the MRI tissue (13.32 cm3) (P1, prep.json). The largest-component rule is an untested suspect for I57, a two-piece 60 mm slab with the lowest OCT tissue fraction (0.404).
items.recommendation: Replace both the intensity-only and texture-only rules with one foreground method validated on cortex (I46, I55, I57) and on the brainstem. Do not force a single component on multi-piece specimens.

items.name: OCT texture specimen mask with auto switch (v1.1, v1.1b sub-options)
items.where: octreg/specimen.py; prep_subject.py --oct-mask auto (fires iff V_int > 1.5 V_MRI and V_tex in 0.5-1.75 V_MRI); --mask-fill-pockets/--mask-fill-holes/--mask-rim-required/--mask-erode-mm; oct150_mask_core.npy
items.what: Min-over-axes directional texture std at 0.04 mm, two-component GMM threshold, rim watershed, pocket reassignment, hole filling.
items.evidence: Brainstem: 28.86 -> 18.05 cm3 (1.355x MRI, one component; port Dice 0.9999993). Overlap gate 0.369 -> 0.59. Structural pose reproducible across seed (0.31 mm / 1.1 deg) and destripe (0.35 mm / 1.4 deg) at the 7 mm cube. But the search margin fell from 1.053 to 1.005 and restarts from 10/12 to 6/12, and the pose moved 0.94 mm / 10.6 deg from the v1 pose with no evidence which is more accurate. P8: >= 5.5 cm3 (30 % of the mask) is still agarose shell and lamellar pockets at any rigid pose; the pocket/hole rules contribute < 0.07 cm3 and the rim rule is a no-op. On I46 (work/v11/tests/mask_I46/result.json) the same recipe keeps 0.28 cm3 against the 0.68 cm3 intensity mask, i.e. it would discard about 59 % of a cortex block; only the auto switch keeps it off DANDI. v1 notes (EXPLAINER §4) already record that pure texture failed on both datasets (only a PNG survives).
items.recommendation: Do not ship as a mode behind a volume-ratio switch. Generalise it (texture fused with intensity, shown to work on I46, I55, I57 and the brainstem) or drop it in favour of the intensity mask plus the adaptive gate. Remove the v1.1b mask sub-flags, which had no measured effect.

items.name: MRI tissue mask (histogram peak-walk with fallback)
items.where: common.histogram_tissue_threshold (rightmost peak, walk left, cut at the first valley with ratio < 0.5, else fallback min(p1, 0.5 x multiotsu[0])); prep.json mri.{valley_ratio, tissue_fraction}
items.what: Air/bath vs tissue split of the MRI, used to mask Otsu statistics and the search overlap.
items.evidence: Plausible hemisphere volumes on 6/9 subjects (386-806 cm3). Fails open on 3/9 (valley_ratio null): I56 2519 cm3 (98.9 % of the volume), I61 1839 cm3 (74.2 %), DANDI I58 1453 cm3 (58.7 %). I61 lands 95.7 mm outside the brain with 12/12 restarts; I56 survived visually. I55 is also null but correct (620.5 cm3). I57's mask is healthy (518 cm3, valley 0.0631) and I57 is still wrong. On the brainstem crop the mask is insensitive to threshold (P8: 0.45 / 0.541 / 0.65 leave region B at 7.26-7.34 cm3). The proposed volume gate (> 1.5 x 806 = about 1210 cm3) would catch all three failures with no false alarm, but it is not implemented, it is hemisphere-specific, and it is meaningless for crops.
items.recommendation: This is the most consequential general gap. Make the rule fail loudly instead of falling back silently, or use one principled foreground model shared with the OCT side. Check foreground volume against the other modality's volume, not against a hemisphere constant.

items.name: Axis-detected destripe (v1.1)
items.where: octreg/destripe.py; prep_subject.py --destripe on/--stripe-axis
items.what: Detect the sectioning axis as the lowest adjacent-plane NCC of high-passed planes, then flat-field along it by normalised convolution (sigma 0.48 mm across, 0.24 mm along).
items.evidence: Brainstem only: axis 2 detected (NCC 0.351 vs 0.630/0.661), period 7.49 voxels = 0.30 mm. x-profile residual 139 -> 50 (test) and 257.6 -> 94.6 (native prep), stripe FFT peak removed, zero fraction unchanged. Effect on the pose is small: R5 vs no-destripe 0.35 mm / 1.4 deg (0.67 mm at the block corners), rim boundary 2.02/1.05 vs 2.02/1.09 mm, restarts 6/12 vs 3/12. P11: a per-section normalisation along axis 2 shows no measurable benefit. I46: the detector is decisive on axis 0 (0.439 vs 0.80; period 16.2 voxels = 0.39 mm; residual 18.8 -> 3.8), but the 'other axes change < 3 %' check fails (y 4.0 -> 4.3, x 5.2 -> 5.6). It was never applied in a DANDI registration. It does not rescue the vessel channel (section-phase modulation 2.54x).
items.recommendation: Keep only as part of one sectioning-artefact step (merged with slab normalisation), driven by the axis detector for all data. Validate by regression on I46/I55 before making it default.

items.name: Global exhaustive FFT masked-NCC search
items.where: octreg/search.py; register.py (--n-rot 8000, x2 mirror, --topk 24, NMS 3 mm AND 10 deg, 0.6 mm level, var_floor 2 %); HANDOFF §5.2
items.what: Scores every translation by FFT for 8000 random SO(3) rotations x {proper, mirrored} per polarity, then keeps the top 24 distinct poses.
items.evidence: Finds I46 (0.09 % of the hemisphere) and I55 in whole hemispheres with no prior. Crop (30 mm) vs whole-hemisphere search gives identical poses on I46 (crop_final2 stretch [1.184, 0.973, 1.034] vs whole_final2 [1.195, 0.975, 1.035]; vessels 166.8 vs 166.6 um). Brainstem v1: 0.1247/0.1184, visually correct body pose. Cost: 44.8 s (brainstem) to 1010 s (I57) per polarity, about 690x cheaper than direct evaluation. Failures trace to the objective, not the search: I61 12/12 at a wrong optimum; the I48 and DANDI I58 landscapes are flat, and I48 had plateaued by 4000/16000 orientations. n_rot, topk, NMS radii and the 0.6 mm level were never swept (I48's plateau and the brainstem's convergence by 4000 orientations suggest 8000 is generous). The search also surfaces the brainstem handedness ambiguity (other handedness 0.1313/0.1250).
items.recommendation: Keep as the centre of the method. Add a sensitivity table (n_rot 2000/4000/8000; level 0.6/0.9 mm) on I46, I55 and the brainstem, and run the true random-pose control.

items.name: Mirror / handedness branch
items.where: search.run (Rs @ diag(1,1,-1)); refine.params_from_matrix (mirror fixed, never optimised); common.rotation_geodesic_deg (returns 180 for opposite determinant)
items.what: Handedness enumerated as a discrete branch in the search and carried unchanged through refinement.
items.evidence: 6 of 9 DANDI runs are mirrored (I38, I46, I48, I56, I58, I62); I55, I57, I61 and the brainstem are not. I46 crop with --no-mirror: top1 0.7328 -> 0.6848, refined 0.7307 -> 0.6853, Dice 0.798/0.829 -> 0.767/0.806, scale degenerates to [0.955, 1, 1]. Cost: 2x search. Brainstem (C.4): undecided. Reported pose: NCC 0.1241, 6/12 restarts, rim 2.02/1.05 mm, y+ face 4.96 mm. Other handedness: NCC 0.1132, 1/12, rim 1.57/1.08 mm, y+ face 1.48 mm. Another other-handedness pose 30.6 mm away scores 0.1358. The headers at face value make the reported pose a mirror. The rotation_deg metric is broken for mirrored transforms (41 fields; for example 129 deg reported vs 2.73 deg true).
items.recommendation: Keep. Output handedness as a discrete result with its score gap, and say 'undecided' when both branches are within noise. Fix rotation_deg before publishing any angle.

items.name: Overlap gate (fixed 0.85, then adaptive)
items.where: register.py:134 MIN_OV = min(min_overlap, max(0.15, 0.8 * V_mri / V_oct)); result.json overlap_gate
items.what: A pose is admissible only if enough of the OCT mask lands on MRI tissue; the threshold scales with the achievable overlap.
items.evidence: Never binds on DANDI (effective 0.850 on all 8 runs that record it; I46_otsu predates the gate). Binds only on the brainstem: 0.369 with the v1 mask, 0.590 with the texture mask. A fixed 0.85 gate rejects every pose there (best achievable about 0.46). The constants 0.8, 0.15 and 0.85 were never swept. In P11, mirrored candidates about 30 mm away passed the 0.59 gate.
items.recommendation: Keep the principle (a fraction of the achievable overlap) as one line and drop the separate 0.85 constant. Show it binding on a controlled case, such as synthetic crops of I46/I55.

items.name: Position-prior paths (--crop-centre/--crop-half-mm, --init-transform)
items.where: register.py; REPORT §2.4; HANDOFF §5.2.6, §9.5.6
items.what: Optional restriction of the search to a box, or skipping search and structural refinement from a given 4x4.
items.evidence: A 30 mm crop vs whole hemisphere gives identical poses on I46 in three pairs and saves about 2 min. The PI states a prior exists in practice, and the brainstem MRI is already cropped (itself a prior). --init-transform was used only to start fine-stage runs (R1, R7, polish); there polarity is evaluated, not optimised (+0.1014 vs -0.1014 at the v1 pose). Never tested as the main mode, and no test of how wrong a prior may be.
items.recommendation: Keep as a documented option. Measure capture range (prior error vs success) on I46/I55, and make the 'prior-free' claim on DANDI only.

items.name: Class polarity selection by refined NCC
items.where: register.py --oct-wm-bright auto (the default is 'no'; run_subject.sh hard-codes auto); result.json polarity_trials
items.what: Search and refinement run for both OCT polarities; the higher refined NCC wins.
items.evidence: The coarse search prefers the wrong polarity on I46 (otsu 0.7411 vs 0.7259). Parser wrong-polarity run: 0.7275 vs 0.7273 at a pose 71 mm away, with a higher WM Dice (0.857 vs 0.803), 0 vessels inside, vessel NCC -0.035 vs 0.301. Refined NCC, winner vs loser: I46 0.7564 vs 0.7300; I55 0.746 vs 0.506; I38 0.478 vs 0.226; I56 0.366 vs 0.248; I62 0.284 vs 0.234; I57 0.512 vs 0.334; I61 0.502 vs 0.321; DANDI I58 0.271 vs 0.232; I48 0.2584 vs 0.2503 (unseparated). Brainstem: v1 0.1014 vs 0.0851; v1.1 0.1241 vs 0.1079, with the other branch 7.2 mm away. The winning polarity varies within one dataset (I46 GM-bright, I55 WM-bright). Correctness is verified only on I46 and I55. Cost: 2x the structural stage.
items.recommendation: Keep. Make auto the default, report the refined-NCC gap, and return 'undecided' when the gap is at noise level (as on I48).

items.name: Coarse-to-fine refinement ladder (rigid -> similarity at 0.6 mm, rigid -> affine at 0.3 mm, affine at 0.15 mm; candidates 24 -> 8 -> 3 -> 1)
items.where: octreg/refine.py (Refiner, Adam with physical learning rates, best-data-loss return); register.py; HANDOFF §5.3
items.what: Degrees of freedom opened stage by stage, with candidate pruning between levels.
items.evidence: I46 structural pose is 1.36 mm (corner mean) from the oracle affine; about 72 % of that is the depth scale (0.98 mm by arithmetic). The refined NCC it produces is the quantity that decides polarity on all subjects. It is the only pose-producing stage accepted on the brainstem. Never ablated: opening the affine at 0.6 mm, a direct affine from the search pose, and the pruning counts. Structural restarts converge 8-12/12 on every DANDI run, including the wrong ones.
items.recommendation: Keep. Add one ablation (direct affine at 0.15 mm from the search pose) to justify the ladder, and describe it in three sentences.

items.name: Scale prior and clamps
items.where: refine.py loss (1 - NCC) + reg*(sum ls^2 + sum sh^2), reg 2.0, ls/sh clamps +-0.15 (scale 0.861-1.162); vascular stage reg 0.5, clamp 0.3
items.what: An absolute prior on log-scale and shear, so a stage cannot buy scale its evidence cannot see.
items.evidence: I46 loss arithmetic: reaching depth 1.162-1.219 costs 0.045-0.078 of prior, while the whole NCC range available along depth is 0.021, so the structural stage correctly refuses to stretch. Control: reg 0.5 / clamp 0.3 without the vessel channel reaches 265.8 um / f150 0.277, 1.24 mm from the oracle (T0 is 276.5 / 0.254 / 1.362): loosening alone buys nothing. I38 structural depth 0.861 = exp(-0.15), i.e. clamp-saturated; the vascular stage then goes to 0.808. Brainstem: without an absolute prior, surface distance (P5) and MI (P6) run into 22-32 % shrink basins, and 8 of 18 MI chains hit the -0.15 clamp, so the prior is what stops the shrink degeneracy. The reg=0 collapse (T_free_affine) was never logged [UNVERIFIED]. The reg and clamp values were never swept.
items.recommendation: Keep and present it as 'each stage may change only what its evidence can see'. Sweep reg in {0.5, 1, 2, 4} and the clamp on I46, I55 and the brainstem. Write clamp saturation into result.json automatically.

items.name: Vascular channel (MRI local darkness vs OCT Frangi vessel density)

items.what: A third NCC channel added after the structural stage to recover what structure cannot see (the depth scale, sub-mm offset).
items.evidence: I46 (12 um OCT, wrong depth sidecar): ves_seg median 264.7 -> 166.7 um, f150 0.283 -> 0.473 (oracle full fit 0.466, held-out 0.416 +- 0.041); depth stretch 1.026 -> 1.219; 8/8 restarts; moved 1.52 mm. Controls collapse the gain: no vessel channel 265.8 um; depth-flipped density 269.5 um; k-slice-permuted 266.2 um. Design sweep (I46 only): the OCT side must be a density (a Frangi map gives 188-241 um); MRI dark vs MRI Frangi tie (166.7 vs 165.1 um); weight 1-4 insensitive; own Frangi within 4 % of manual ves_seg; Frangi at 12 um is useless (NCC 0.007). I55 (14 um, correct sidecar): moved 0.33 mm, vessel NCC 0.083, 8/8; only the training metric exists there (own vessels 173 -> 141 um). 30-35 um subjects: vessel NCC I38 0.053 (7/8), I56 0.020 (0/8), I62 0.003 (1/8), I57 -0.002 (1/8), I61 0.019 (4/8); I38 spent 5697 s of 7864 s in this stage. The depth-scale claim itself is open: I55 recovers a 0.8570 = 6/7 anisotropy, the single-axis probe shows the vessel metric responding on k rather than on depth [UNVERIFIED], and it is n=1 each way.
items.recommendation: Remove from the core method. At most keep it as an optional, gated independent channel, or as an evaluation verifier for sub-25 um cortex. Before claiming the depth-scale result, run the I46-at-14,12,12 / I55-at-12,12,12 re-prep test.

audit_benchmark.summary:
I did a read-only check of the AutoDL server: file listings, NIfTI/OME-TIFF headers, prep.json, result.json and logs. I edited nothing and started no jobs. My local scratch files are deleted.

Everything needed to prep all 10 pairs from scratch is on the server. That is 9 DANDI subjects (I38, I46, I48, I55, I56, I57, I58, I61, I62) plus Xiangrui's I58 brainstem pair. All 81 files in the multi-subject manifest match their declared sizes and there are no partial downloads. Size is the only integrity check, though: the multi-subject manifest has no sha256 (only the I46 starter manifest does), and the earlier corrupt I58 30-degree file had the right size and still failed its gzip CRC. The raw data takes 63 G (DANDI, including a 2.76 G `.corrupt.bak` copy) plus 13 G (Xiangrui). All of `work` is 207 G, of which the 9 DANDI prep dirs are about 137 G. The disk has 1.2 T free.

The code on the server matches local HEAD db2282e (md5 checked on octreg/*.py and the 5 main scripts). But no prep.json records a code version, arguments or time. All 9 DANDI preps were made on 08-20/21 by the tree from before git. Xiangrui's final prep was made on 09-14 by code equal to HEAD.

**Blocker for label-based numbers.** For the seven 0.12 mm DANDI subjects, the EPIC MRI header does not match the label files. The labels (BA, vessel and whole-hemisphere files all agree with each other) describe a hemisphere about 70-77 mm left-right. The MRI header instead gives 168-192 mm left-right, and for I38 the label arrays are also axis-permuted relative to the MRI.

So every label-based check on these subjects was sampled through a broken mapping: labels4, BA labels, MRI vessels, Dice, "0 % of the BA label inside the block" and vessel n_inside = 0. The registrations themselves are not affected.

I did a header-only re-check (block centre from result.json, pushed through a label file with the same array shape):
- **I56:** the block centre lands 0.4 mm from the BA label's crop box. HANDOFF says 65.9 mm, so that "contradiction" looks like a header artefact.
- **I48:** the block centre is about 44 mm from the MRI vessel-annotation crop box, which leans towards the pose being wrong.

Both estimates need the label data loaded to confirm. Two more evaluation problems:
- **OCT vessel segmentations:** for I38 and I48 they are not on the OCT grid (crops). For I46 the depth offset of 0 or 66 slices is still undecided.
- **Dice denominator:** it uses the whole OCT class count, so Dice collapses whenever labels cover only part of the block.

**Compute budget (serial, from logs).**
- DANDI prep: 188-1459 s each, 8530 s in total (2.4 h). About 60-800 s of each is label mapping, which should move to the evaluation step.
- DANDI registration (v1 settings, which are still HEAD defaults for these data): 1125-7864 s each, 23638 s in total (6.6 h). I38's vascular stage alone took 5697 s.
- Xiangrui one-command chain (both handedness candidates, QC and export): 27.5 min, 32 GB peak.
- QC on whole-hemisphere MRI was never run; I assume a few minutes per pair.

That gives about 10 h serial for a full run, one heavy job at a time (the 62 GB container limit has frozen the instance before). Re-running the evaluation from the stored transforms after the frame fix would take roughly 1-2 h.

**Metrics.**
- **Label-based** (after the frame fix):
  - GM/WM agreement restricted to labelled voxels: 8 subjects, not I62.
  - Fraction of the BA label inside the registered block: all 9 DANDI blocks are sample BrocaAreaS01.
  - MRI manual vessels against the OCT vessel distance map, with a random-shift control: I46, I55, and the others once n_inside is 20 or more.
  - OCT ves_seg vessels: I46 only.
  - Depth scale against the physical prior: I46 against I55.
- **Label-free** (all 10 pairs): search margin, polarity margin, handedness margin, restart convergence, vascular acceptance gate, stretch plausibility, overlap volumes, distance to the distinct runner-up, MI landscape shape, and the export round-trip check. The boundary (rim) check only means something for whole-specimen OCT like Xiangrui's, not for cortex blocks whose faces are cuts. None of these separates right from wrong on its own: I58 and I61 converge 12/12 and are wrong, and I57/I61 have NCC around 0.5 and are wrong. They should be calibrated against the label verdicts on the 9 DANDI pairs.

audit_code.summary:
Audit of octreg at db2282e (package 13 files / 2,815 lines; scripts 53 .py + 19 .sh + 1 .json / ~5,600 lines), read in full, with read-only checks of result.json args and prep.json on the server.

1. Most of the code is not the method. Every reported number comes from two entry points: scripts/prep_subject.py and scripts/register.py. They use about two thirds of the package: common, search, refine, the two-class split in features, evaluate, parts of vascular, plus specimen and destripe for I58. The QC/export tools are qc_fine.py, export_registration.py and check_export_header.py. About 45 of the 73 scripts are legacy, experimental-negative or one-off: the I46 v0 driver, the I46-only prep chain, the I46 validation suite, the parser/distillation branch, reference-pose forensics, brainstem one-offs, 10 recovery drivers and 5 v1.1 run plans. Most of them cannot run on current prep outputs (they need oct12_affine, oct24 or oct_ves_dist48_z0, which prep_subject.py never writes). Three modules are dead weight for the method: parser.py, synth.py (except gaussian_blur3d, which features.py imports) and nonrigid.py. fine.py (675 lines, 22 CLI flags) is a measured negative: rejected in every I58 run, and on I46/I55 it passes its own gates but makes the labelled metrics worse.

2. The published default path is less general than the docs say. Every reported run passes `--oct-wm-bright auto` explicitly; the default 'no' is wrong for 7 of the 9 DANDI subjects plus the brainstem. The OCT two-class map is NOT bias-flattened (only the MRI map is), and its blur is in voxels, not mm. The slab normalisation assumes array axis 0 and a 1.2 mm section period: measured periods are about 3x shorter on I46/I56, and on I58 the sectioning axis is axis 2. The texture-mask auto rule compares the OCT block volume to the whole MRI tissue volume, so it can only fire when the MRI is cropped to the block. On I46 the texture mask would keep 0.28 of about 0.68 cm3 of tissue. The foreground threshold fails open (silent keep-everything fallback) on I61, DANDI I58 and I56. The vascular stage and all its gate thresholds come from I46/I55/I58 numbers, and the section-phase gate has never been exercised. `--destripe on` would stop with SystemExit on 14 um spacing like I55 (worked out from the code, not run). map_labels_to_grid still mis-pairs label axes on the six 0.12 mm subjects. prep ignores the OCT NIfTI orientation (layout letters), which is the only reason export_registration.py exists.

3. Mechanisms that do the same job:
   - Sectioning/bias normalisation, 4-5 of them: slab normalise, destripe, the MRI 10 mm flattening, the fine 3 mm flattening, the archived P11 normalisation.
   - Foreground masks, more than 10.
   - Polarity, 5 mechanisms; handedness, 4.
   - Pose-difference metrics: a fixed 7 mm cube (rotation broken for mirrored poses) versus block corners.
   - QC figures and summaries, 7+ each.
   - Low-level helpers: pooling, erosion, largest component, Gaussian, MI-32, perturbation and GridDisp are each written 2-5 times.

4. Minimal reproduction path:
   - DANDI: prep_subject.py (defaults + annotation flags) then register.py --oct-wm-bright auto, then viz_result.py and summarize.py.
   - Xiangrui I58: run_xiangrui_i58.sh = prep with --oct-mask auto --destripe on --skip-vessels, register without the fine stage, qc_fine, export and header check, and the other handedness via an inline affine flip plus --no-mirror.
   - Reproducibility is only partly shown. R8/R9 re-ran register.py bit-identically from the STORED DANDI preps, and the one-command I58 run reproduces R5 to 0.00 mm. But the DANDI preps were made by older prep code: the I46 prep has no float16 gain (octv level ~100 vs I55 ~14k) and was never regenerated.

5. Suggested general method, a few steps:
   - loader that uses header affines;
   - one sectioning flat-field along the detected axis;
   - one foreground estimator with explicit failure, applied to both modalities;
   - the same flattened two-class maps on both sides;
   - FFT search over rotation x {handedness, relative polarity};
   - rigid then similarity then affine with a stated scale prior;
   - boundary-agreement QC calibrated on the labelled pairs;
   - export in the input file frames.
   Vessels become optional. The fine stage, parser, nonrigid and ~50 scripts are archived.

items.name: common.oct_slab_normalize and prep's slab window/threshold formula
items.where: octreg/common.py L181-211 (defaults tissue_thresh=30, window=100, float16 gain 16384 and cap 60000); scripts/prep_subject.py L140-146 (thr_raw = 0.5*Otsu of raw[::4,::8,::8]>0; window = max(10, round(1200/sp_z)))
items.what: Per slice along array axis 0: median of voxels above a raw threshold (only if >2000 voxels), divide by it, multiply by a running mean of the medians over 'window' slices. Output float16 with tissue median scaled to ~16384. Writes nothing itself; its output feeds oct150.npy and octv.npy in prep.
items.evidence: Axis-0 assumption: on I58 the sectioning axis is array axis 2 (P3; the axis-0 correction removes 1.5 %, P11 norm probe). Window formula: comment says 1.2 mm = one section period at 12 um, but the measured period is 33 slices on I46 (window 100) and 12 slices on I56 (window 34) (HANDOFF 5.1.7, 7.2.9). Function defaults 30/100 are I46 values. On the I58 NIfTI the 0.5*Otsu raw threshold is 0.00096, i.e. everything >0 (server prep.json). Mixed provenance: I46 octv level ~100 (prep 2026-08-20 10:04, before the gain trick) vs I55 ~14,388 (server check), so DANDI preps come from different prep versions. P11: undoing it or replacing it with per-section / tile flat-field changes structural NCC by <=0.0004 at P_R5. The slab step itself was never ablated on DANDI.
items.recommendation: Replace with one sectioning-artefact step that takes axis and period from the data (destripe.detect_stripe_axis plus its FFT period), or drop it after a DANDI ablation. Keep the float16 gain only as a storage detail. Re-prep all benchmark pairs with one code version.

Class defaults n_rot 3000, topk 32, min_overlap 0.85 differ from register.py's 8000/24.

items.name: refine.py (Refiner, compose, params_from_matrix, masked_ncc)
items.where: octreg/refine.py (148 lines); scripts/register.py L153-164, L229; subclassed/used by vascular.py, fine.py, nonrigid.py
items.what: Point-based masked NCC of MRI features sampled at OCT tissue points (mask > 0.05). Parameters: rotation vector, translation about the block centre, log-scales, shears, mirror flag. Adam with lr 0.02 rad / 0.3 mm / 0.01 / 0.01 and cosine schedule. Absolute clamps +-0.15 and regulariser reg*(|ls|^2+|sh|^2), default reg 2.0. Returns the best data loss.
items.evidence: Parameterisation round-trips; autograd matches finite differences (implementation_review_record impl:B). Scale prior is load-bearing: at reg 2 the prior costs 0.045-0.078 to reach the I46 depth scale while the whole depth-axis NCC range is 0.021. I38 depth stretch 0.861 = exp(-0.15) is clamp-saturated. Loosening the prior alone gains nothing (265.8 vs 276.5 um) (HANDOFF 5.3.3-5.3.4). Clamps are absolute, which is why fine.py wraps a delta refiner.
items.recommendation: Keep. Make the clamps relative to the start pose inside Refiner, which removes fine.py's _DeltaRefiner. State the prior once as a physical scale bound.

Pose effect small: R5 vs no-destripe 0.35 mm / 1.4 deg (0.67 mm at block corners). I46: detection decisive on axis 0 (0.439 vs 0.80, period 0.39 mm) but destripe never applied on DANDI, so its effect on registration outside I58 is untested. Clip floor 1.0 assumes the 16384 gain level (I46 octv level ~100 would clip ~1 %). hp_sigma_vox 3 and the 60-plane detrend are voxel counts tuned at 0.04 mm (impl:C).

scores.fatal_or_major_problems:
1. Too many untested changes land in one release candidate. Unmasked OCT channels, OCT-side flattening, the h rule on 0.12 mm MRIs, the no-largest-component cleanup applied to the MRI as well, per-hypothesis top-12, rho 0.8 instead of 0.85, header frames and divide-form section gain all change together. A regression on I46/I55 cannot be attributed to one of them, and A10 reverts run only after a failure. Land them as a staged sequence, with a regression check against the stored v1 transforms after each change.
2. There is no automatic 'undecided' rule. Gaps are reported but never interpreted, so a new user gets numbers without guidance, and I48-type ties go out looking like normal results.
3. Agarose OCT and bath MRI are handled only by a user-supplied mask. That keeps the method simple but moves the work to users. The brainstem relies on the rho gate with an over-inclusive mask (v1 did this successfully).
4. Step 3 (section gain at native resolution) uses a foreground threshold defined in step 2 at h, so the order of these two steps needs spelling out.
5. Two budget items are hard to justify: 22 h of ANTs on whole hemispheres and 15 h of A13 seeds. Trim them or limit them to 3 pairs.
6. The 'keep all components >= 1 %' rule on the MRI may keep bath fragments. They are flagged but not removed.

scores.strengths:
It has the best user-facing semantics:
- status OK / AMBIGUOUS / UNRELIABLE with reason codes;
- a decisions[] audit trail in result.json;
- docs/statuses.md telling the user what to do for each reason;
- every discrete ambiguity exported as a ranked alternative in the input frames.

Other strengths:
- Using --init to restrict the same search, instead of skipping it, is the right single prior mechanism.
- The deterministic super-Fibonacci grid makes bit-identical reruns (A7) achievable.
- Anti-aliased resampling removes the integer-factor bugs (the 14 um SystemExit and round(12.5)).
- Vessels are isolated in an extras/ module that the core never imports.
- The phantom tests are the most thorough of the three: dark bath, bright bath, textured agarose, all-tissue crop, two-piece specimen, a non-separable case that must fail, and a mirror-symmetric phantom that must come out AMBIGUOUS.
- Parameters.md is generated from config.py, and every figure caption carries a git hash.
- Acceptance A2 ('no silent wrong pose') is the right goal.

The strongest documentation and presentation plan:
- METHOD.md, conventions.md, benchmark.md and limitations.md;
- tables T1-T5 and 7 figures, all generated by bench/report.py, with no hand edits;
- a human visual sign-off CSV, which fixes the problem of verdicts read by an AI from figures;
- explicit honesty rules (report confirmed/unresolved/failed counts, restarts described as basin width, no absolute NCC threshold, prior-free claims limited to DANDI).

Other strengths:
- Module split (io / grid / normalize / foreground / structure / search / refine / pipeline / qc / config / cli) is clean, under 1,800 lines.
- Ablations are YAML config diffs, never code branches.
- Relative clamps remove fine._DeltaRefiner.
- Tests include an autograd-vs-finite-difference check and an export test ported from check_export_header.
- Manifest with sha256 and a pinned dandiset version; serial queue with a watchdog.
- E0 evaluation repair comes first.
- Pre-registered config and thresholds; baselines cover ANTs, NiftyReg, MIND, the authors' affine, and v1.1 as shipped.
- A11 decides the vessel question with the corrected spacing instead of by assertion.
scores.fatal_or_major_problems:
1. The decision rule is not sound. Basin sigma is the std of refined NCC over 12 restarts that return within 1 mm. Converged restarts give sigma near zero, so almost any gap passes 3 sigma. Stable wrong basins (I61 and DANDI I58 at 12/12) would come out 'decided', and the claimed 'I48 undecided' does not follow from this rule. It also keeps the 12-restart machinery that the evidence says is anti-correlated with correctness, which adds a concept and compute.
2. The foreground estimator is a cascade (valley, then GMM, then texture for OCT without a valley). That is a hidden mode switch, and the texture branch has only been validated on I58.
3. It does not exploit the score-sign duality. Polarity is searched as separate swapped-channel hypotheses with top-24 each, so search cost stays about 2x.
4. The override surface (--config, --set key=value, and a data card holding a 'corrected' I46 spacing) makes per-pair tuning easy; it is policed only by acceptance criterion 6.
5. Acceptance pre-specifies outcomes: brainstem handedness 'must be undecided'.
6. The synthetic target (>= 95 % within 0.3 mm) is drawn from the same MRIs.
7. Baseline compute is optimistic: ANTs with 48 multi-starts on a whole 0.12 mm hemisphere at about 1 h per pair on CPU. The about 4-5 day serial plan will likely overrun.

must_have: One obvious entry point: `octreg register OCT MRI -o OUT` (<= ~6 options: spacing for header-less TIFF, optional masks, optional prior, device, seed) plus `octreg apply`. All method constants live in one frozen, documented Params/config with a unit and provenance for each; any override is recorded and marks the run nondefault.

Relative polarity obtained as the sign of the score in the same FFT pass (make OCT channels u and 1-u, unmasked; the weight carries support). Handedness searched as a discrete branch. Every run refines and exports the best candidate of every hypothesis. A CPU unit test asserts that swapping channels gives score -S.

The same mm-based two-class function applied to both modalities, and one foreground function applied to both. The foreground function returns an explicit status and never silently keeps everything. No largest-component rule. Kept or deleted according to a pre-declared ablation, not by default.
At most one sectioning step: detected axis and measured period, recorded no-op when nothing is decisive, with a pre-declared deletion rule if an ablation on I46/I55/brainstem shows no effect.
The absolute scale prior and the rigid->similarity->affine ladder kept as the only pose-producing refinement, with clamp saturation written to result.json.

Outputs written directly in the input file frames: 4x4 in both directions, LTA/ITK, overlays in both grids, a hypothesis table. result.json records git hash, argv, params hash, input sha256, spacing source, per-stage runtime and peak RAM/GPU.

Clean split: the installed package contains only the method. Label mapping (fixed), metrics, random-pose null, baselines, ablations and the report generator live in bench/. Legacy code is preserved at an archive git tag before deletion.
Stage 0 before any method change: repair the label frame and re-score the stored v1 transforms, so every acceptance criterion references honest verdicts.
Staged migration: land each merged change as its own commit, with a regression check against stored v1 transforms on I46, I55 and the brainstem, so a regression can be attributed to one change.
must_not: No per-dataset or per-pair method flags or modes: no --oct-wm-bright, --no-mirror, --destripe, --oct-mask auto, and no auto switch keyed on whole-MRI volume ratios. Config overrides (--set key=value) must not become a per-pair tuning channel.

Do not ship the fine stage, the vascular channel in the core, the parser/synth, nonrigid, the MI landscape or MIND in the package. At most, vessels go in an isolated extras module that the core never imports.

Do not gate or declare correctness on restart counts, restart-NCC spread, absolute NCC, raw top1/top2 margins, or thresholds fitted to the same few pairs they are evaluated on (for example LOSO-calibrated Ashman D on n = 9).
Do not derive a 'decided/undecided' noise scale from converged restarts, which gives sigma near zero in stable wrong basins.
No silent fallbacks: foreground, spacing, 4-D squeeze, header orientation.
Do not land all merged changes (foreground rewrite, OCT flattening, unmasked channels, new grid/NMS, flat field, header frames) in one untested release candidate.

Do not grow the search budget (for example covering-angle grids of 33k orientations per handedness) or add texture features on every volume without a measured accuracy gain; either could multiply benchmark cost on the 62 GB / one-GPU server.
Do not run two heavy jobs in parallel, copy volumes or caches to the local Mac, or overwrite the old prep caches.
Do not keep label/annotation mapping inside prep or registration, or report any Dice for the 0.12 mm subjects before the frame repair.
Do not pre-specify experimental outcomes as acceptance criteria (for example 'brainstem handedness must be undecided'), and do not hand-edit figures or use AI-read figures as verdicts.
Do not keep package code that no reported number exercises, or leave stale README pointers to superseded scripts.

scores.design: minimal (octreg 1.0 minimal core: two-class maps, one exhaustive search over pose x handedness x polarity, one prior-bounded affine ladder)
scores.strengths:
It changes the least evidence, and the changes it makes are ones that can be checked.

- **Search, ladder and scale prior** are kept almost unchanged: the prior at 2 with clamp 0.15, the ladder, and the adaptive overlap gate (0.8·min(1,V_M/V_O) gives 0.37 on the brainstem crop, matching v1's 0.369).
- **Polarity duality is correct.** I checked it at db2282e: the OCT channels are [s·m, (1−s·m)·m] (features.py L51-65), and the search and refiner score the mean channel-weighted NCC. Swapping the OCT classes therefore negates the score exactly when the mask is binary. One search pass gives all four hypotheses, the same candidates as v1's two-pass auto mode at half the cost. It also correctly notes that the MRI second channel carries the outline, which explains the brainstem channels [-0.017, 0.220].
- **Sectioning step reproduces v1.** A window of 3 measured periods gives the current windows on I46 (100 slices = 3.03P) and I56 (34 = 2.83P), and moves the step to axis 2 on I58. On DANDI subjects sectioned along axis 0 it should reproduce v1 prep, and it is a recorded no-op when the axis is not decisive.
- **Foreground threshold is unchanged from v1.** No regression on the six MRIs with a valley or on I55's fallback. The fail-open case gets a flag.
- **Unvalidated steps can be deleted.** Rule R9 deletes OCT flattening (A1), the sectioning gain (A3) or the extra ladder stage (A6) if they are not needed. Rule R10 reverts each merged step on its own if it breaks I46, I55 or the brainstem.
- **Useful evidence experiments:**
  - A11 oracle-foreground ablation on I56, I57, I61 and DANDI I58 separates mask failures from objective failures;
  - A12 spacing variants decide whether the vessel depth-scale result is really a metadata error;
  - a random admissible-pose null.
- **Evaluation and scope.** Stage 0 label-frame repair runs before any verdict. I58 at 30 deg is an extra row. Restarts, absolute NCC and margin are never used as gates, with the right counterexamples (I61 and DANDI I58 at 12/12, I62 at 0.28, I55 margin 1.004). scores.fatal_or_major_problems:
1. **Validated components on confirmed pairs are replaced by machinery with no evidence on any dataset:**
   - **Joint GMM foreground for both modalities** (log intensity plus directional texture, border-enrichment background, Bhattacharyya ≥1.0, E ≥1.5). On I46 it replaces a peak-walk that works. Texture alone kept 0.28 of 0.68 cm3 there, and border enrichment is doubtful for cortex blocks whose OCT FOV faces cut through tissue. MRI texture at 0.12 mm has never been computed. A plain GMM is not the P1 recipe (watershed rim, pockets) that gave 18.05 cm3 on the brainstem.
   - **Log-domain in-sheet flat field applied to DANDI by default.** Destripe has never run in a DANDI registration, and on I46 it failed its own 'other axes change <3 %' check.
   - **Super-Fibonacci covering-angle rule.** It roughly doubles the search on I38 and I57 (about 33k orientations per handedness) with no evidence that finer sampling helps: I48 had plateaued by 4000 of 16000.
2. **Many new thresholds with no provenance:** E 1.5, Bhattacharyya 1.0, coverage 0.7, V ratio 1.3, B ≥8, component 5 %, and an Ashman-D cut fitted on the same 9 pairs whose verdicts are themselves uncertain. Leave-one-subject-out on n=9 is weak.
3. **No deletion rule for unvalidated steps.** If regression fails, it falls back to the old window instead of dropping the step.
4. **A2 may be unachievable** (I57 has no diagnosed mechanism), with no plan for that case.
5. **Same brainstem risk as the other designs.** Per-hypothesis retention plus choosing the winner on raw refined S can promote the 0.1358 mirrored 5.4 %-shrink pose over R5 (0.1241). The jackknife would call it AMBIGUOUS, but the primary transform would still flip.
6. **Confirmed pairs could turn UNRELIABLE.** If the new foreground or contrast rules misfire, I46 or I55 become UNRELIABLE; A3 tolerates one.
7. **About 90 h of queue.**

Overall: the most general in intent, but the weakest on 'every kept component is supported by evidence', and the greatest risk of losing currently validated behaviour.

scores.design: publication (octreg 1.0: search on two-class maps, 8-step paper design with data cards, baselines and pre-registration)

must_have: Stage 0 before any method decision: repair the label-to-MRI frame for the seven 0.12 mm subjects (map by array axes to the same-shape label file; for I57/I61 choose flips by label-on-tissue fraction). Re-score the stored v1 transforms. Use Dice restricted to labelled voxels plus BA-inside fraction. Set verdicts with a pre-declared random-admissible-pose null and human-verified figures. The success count and every calibration depend on this.

Implement relative polarity as the sign of the one score map. At db2282e the OCT channels are [s*m, (1-s*m)*m], so swapping them negates the masked NCC exactly for a binary mask. One search pass then yields all four handedness x polarity hypotheses. Refine and export the best transform of each hypothesis, with its score, in the input file frames.

Choose between hypotheses with the same penalised loss the refiner optimises (NCC plus scale prior), as v1's polarity choice did, not raw NCC. Explicitly test the known brainstem competitor from REPORT C.4: a mirrored pose with 5.4 % shrink, 30.6 mm away, scoring 0.1358 against R5's 0.1241 on the 0.15 mm objective. The v1 joint keep-3 dropped it, and per-hypothesis retention will keep it. Report the outcome.

Report ambiguity as a first-class output: all four refined hypothesis scores, delta_polarity, delta_handedness, a size-normalised search decisiveness and the distance to the distinct runner-up. Any 'undecided' label must come from a data-internal noise scale, such as a spatial block jackknife. That scale must be shown on synthetic symmetric controls to call symmetric cases undecided, and must come out decided on I46/I55 and undecided on I48 polarity and brainstem handedness.

Report per-OCT-axis scale clamp saturation and identifiability. Clamp saturation fires on I38 (depth exp(-0.15)). An identifiability check should mark I46 depth as unidentifiable (dNCC 0.021), because clamp saturation alone misses I46: its structural stretch is 1.026.

Sectioning handling: detect the axis and period from the data (I46 axis 0 at 0.39 mm; I58 axis 2 at 0.30 mm), and make the step a recorded no-op when detection is not decisive. If a gain is kept, use a 3-measured-period window, which reproduces the current I46 (100 slices) and I56 (34 slices) windows. Pre-declare that the step is deleted if an ablation on I46, I55 and the brainstem shows no effect.

One foreground rule applied to both modalities. It keeps the v1 peak-walk threshold wherever a valley exists (no regression on I46, I38, I62, I48, I57), replaces the silent fail-open with an explicit flag, and allows multi-piece specimens. Any replacement (GMM, texture) must first pass: I46 OCT mask >= 0.9x the intensity mask, I55 unchanged, and an oracle-mask ablation on I56, I57, I61 and DANDI I58 that separates mask failures from objective failures.

Handle metadata honestly. The sidecar spacing is the primary input. I46 at 12/12/14 um and I55 at 12/12/12 um run as declared variants, which decide whether the dropped vascular depth-scale gain was a metadata artefact. DANDI I58 at 30 deg runs as an extra row next to the 10 deg failure case.

Take the vascular stage out of the core, but keep the I46 vessel-level result reproducible from an archive tag or an optional extension. Set a stated evidence bar for re-entry (gain on >= 2 labelled vessel pairs, e.g. adding I45/I60). Scope the release claim to mm-level placement.

Pre-declared regression acceptance against the v1 structural pose:
- I46 and I55: Dice within 0.02; pose within about 0.5-1 mm on OCT mask points.
- A per-step revert rule.
- Explicit regression on the 0.12 mm subjects for the level change (v1 0.6/0.24/0.12 to 0.6/0.3/0.15).
- Re-prep all 10 pairs from raw at one tag, with sha256-verified inputs and the git hash and argv in prep.json and result.json.
- I57, I61, DANDI I58 and I48 appear in the main table.

Use header affines for NIfTI and report handedness as 'unknown' for frame-less TIFF. Export in the input file frames with a raw-data frame test: Spearman at the pose against the header-axis-flip controls, as in check_export_header.

Report boundary agreement only when a data-internal rule says the OCT outline is a real specimen surface (the fraction of OCT boundary away from FOV faces). It is descriptive, not accuracy; it was never calibrated and it favours the other handedness on I58.

Add a synthetic known-transform benchmark (pose, handedness, polarity, spacing error, stripes, embedding) and a true random-pose control. Use them to measure capture range and the calibration of the decision rules; no accuracy claims from synthetic data.
must_not: Do not accept, reject or rank poses by absolute NCC, restart convergence counts, raw top1/top2 margin or a hemisphere-volume constant. Counterexamples: I61 and I57 score about 0.50 and are wrong; I62 scores 0.28 and is correct; I61 and DANDI I58 converge 12/12 and are wrong; the I55 margin is 1.004 and I55 is correct.

Do not use the refined-NCC spread of converged restarts as the noise scale for decided/undecided. It is optimiser noise inside one basin, it is undefined when restarts do not converge (other handedness 1/12), and it would call the brainstem handedness decided.
Do not decide between hypotheses on raw data NCC while the refiner optimises NCC plus the scale prior. Shrink poses (P5/P6; the 0.1358 mirrored 5.4 %-shrink brainstem pose) exploit exactly that gap.

Do not ship the texture specimen mask, or an intensity+texture GMM, as a default or behind an automatic switch until it passes I46 and I55. The texture recipe keeps 0.28 of 0.68 cm3 on I46. The volume-ratio switch can only fire on MRI crops. A plain GMM is not the validated P1 recipe (watershed rim, pockets) that gave 18.05 cm3.

Do not change the foreground threshold definition (log histogram, GMM fallback, new cleanup) on the confirmed pairs without regression. I55 is correct under the current no-valley fallback, and six MRIs have healthy valleys.

Do not apply the I58-derived in-sheet destripe field, or any new flat-field form, to DANDI by default without an I46/I55 regression. On I46 destripe failed its own other-axes check, and slab normalisation was never ablated.

Do not correct per-pair metadata in the primary benchmark (e.g. I46 depth set to 14 um in a data card) using sibling, oracle or label-derived evidence. Keep sidecar values primary and run corrections as declared variants.

Do not introduce new thresholds or sampling rules fitted to, or motivated only by, the 9 DANDI pairs they are evaluated on without leave-one-subject-out calibration, freezing and a stated provenance. Examples: contrast cut, coverage 0.7, Bhattacharyya 1.0, border enrichment 1.5, a covering-angle rule that doubles the search on I38/I57 despite I48 plateauing at 4000 orientations.

Do not keep in the method or CLI: the fine stage (rejected in 13/13 I58 configurations and harmful on I46/I55), the parser, self-distillation, MIND, nonrigid, the MI landscape as QC, the vascular gate constants, or the section-phase modulation gate (never exercised).
Do not drop the MRI foreground multiplication from the MRI class channels. It carries the outline that places the brainstem.

Do not report Dice, BA-inside or vessel numbers for the 0.12 mm subjects before the label-frame repair. Do not keep the Dice whose denominator is the whole OCT class count. Do not keep the 7 mm-cube rotation metric that is invalid for mirrored transforms.
Do not claim prior-free search on the brainstem (its MRI is already a crop), physical handedness for DANDI TIFF blocks or the brainstem, or vessel-level / depth-scale accuracy for the release core.
Do not remove the stated failures (I57, I61, DANDI I58 at 10 deg, I48) from the benchmark, and do not patch them with pair-specific masks or flags presented as part of the general method.
